versions.changelog:
Updated to work with the Openclaw Projects and Build a dev team skills more cohesively   |   https://clawhub.ai/encryptshawn/openclaw-projects   |  https://clawhub.ai/encryptshawn/build-dev-team
- Expanded agent workspace requirements: now references HEARTBEAT.md and AGENTS.md in addition to USER.md and TOOLS.md, specifying their contents and operational roles.
- Added structured format and strict rules for HEARTBEAT.md to guide queue checking, including model selection, minimal reasoning, and multi-project participation.
- Introduced protocols for ClickUp task management as an alternative to Asana, using the same heartbeat structure.
- Clarified that heartbeat runs must always use the cheapest available model, explicitly disallowing fallback to primary models to conserve resources.
- Defined clear failure-handling behavior for heartbeat sessions: fail cheap, log, and never escalate or retry with higher-cost models.

**Summary: Credentials and scheduling are now strictly externalized; workflow clarified as guidance only.**

- Updated to clarify this skill never accesses or manages credentials or tokens; all authentication is handled by dependency skills (Git, Asana).
- Noted that the 30-minute heartbeat is triggered and scheduled by the OpenClaw platform, not by the skill itself.
- Added detailed sections on the trust and workspace file model, explicitly stating that USER.md and TOOLS.md are operator-managed and never contain secrets.
- Restructured documentation around dependency skill usage and clarified that this skill only provides workflow instructions, never executes API calls or stores sensitive information.
- No behavioral changes to developer task workflow or inter-agent coordination.

**Expanded to support heartbeat task queue checks and API contract coordination across multiple projects.**

- Added Asana heartbeat protocol: every 30 minutes, checks the correct dev queue (FE/BE) for each active project in USER.md and picks up ready tasks.
- Introduced sessions_send protocol for inter-agent coordination: now required for PR handoffs, API contract sharing, and escalation to other roles.
- Clarified FE/BE role separation: branch naming, repo access, and usage of authentication env vars from TOOLS.md.
- Added workflows for handling API contract readiness and frontend/backend interoperation (sessions_send between dev-fe and dev-be).
- Updated blocker escalation and dependency handling: always comment in Asana and sessions_send to PM/Engineer as appropriate.
- Refined task workflow details and emphasized multi-project support for developer agents.

Initial release: defines developer task workflow and team protocols for managed software projects.

- Clarifies FE/BE developer roles and ownership boundaries within project teams.
- Outlines task lifecycle: assignment, spec review, active work, blocker escalation, self-check, PR creation, QA handoff, and completion.
- Specifies branch naming conventions per role.
- Details required external skills (Git, Asana, tech stack skills) with this skill focused on coordination and workflow.
- Provides explicit escalation and status update procedures to facilitate efficient teamwork.
- you need to install your choice of git, asana and developer tech skills
